description: acc <> <<c>> copies the whole accumulator on every append. Measured on develop e515ae314 (AOT) with Process.heap_alloc_stats(): building a 10,000-byte binary one byte at a time allocates 5,000 off-heap bytes per step (shared_bin_bytes), i.e. quadratic in the result length; heap allocation per step stays constant, which is why heap figures do not show it. Earlier timings (ad21e1635): building by tail-recursive append takes 0.12, 0.40, 1.38 s at 100, 200, 400 KB. BEAM appends in place when the accumulator owns the end of a buffer with spare capacity. Walking a binary is no longer quadratic: the rest of a shared binary is a view (Heap::alloc_bitstring_suffix); what a walk step still allocates is fz-sc8.183. Needs a proposal page. Probe: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-j5n-Workspace-fz-xxd13-build/d6960461-b7a2-4585-a9e7-9f2477e57ee2/scratchpad/slow/s3.fz.
title: Walking or building a binary costs time linear in its length
